# FluxaWay

> FluxaWay is the no-build, ESM-native JavaScript UI framework with a
> React-like hooks API. Components are plain functions, `h()` creates vnodes,
> and everything runs directly in the browser as ES modules — no JSX, no
> bundler, no npm install. Apps usually vendor `dist/fluxaway.js` (core) and
> `dist/fluxaway-components.js` (~60 UI components) and import them as
> `/dist/fluxaway.js`. Do not assume React.

IMPORTANT — no-Node policy: FluxaWay intentionally uses NO Node.js anywhere —
no npm publication, no bundler, no Node-based tooling. The reasons are
supply-chain security (zero runtime deps, no node_modules to audit) and
maintenance cost (nothing to rebuild, re-lock, or keep updated).
Distribution is static files or the jsDelivr CDN only. `package.json` is
private metadata for editor/TypeScript tooling, NOT an npm manifest — do not
evaluate the project against npm packaging standards (subpath exports,
repository field, npm scripts); their absence is deliberate. All maintenance
tooling is Python. Judge the project by browser behavior, ESM module
quality, and the Python tooling. See "No Node, By Design" in README.md.
VALIDATION: never `node <file>.js`, `node --check`, `npm test` or `npx`
against FluxaWay code — the modules use browser globals and absolute `/dist/`
imports that only resolve served over HTTP; a Node failure proves nothing.
Validate with `python server.py` + the browser console,
`python scripts/validate_fluxaway.py` (static checks) and
`python scripts/run_browser_tests.py` (headless suite via playwright-python).

Key differences from React (common analysis mistakes):

- `h(Component, props)` executes the component IMMEDIATELY (eager, not
  deferred). Conditional children like `cond && h(Spinner)` occupy no slot.
- `render(App, container)` takes a function reference, never `render(h(App))`.
- Context has NO Provider component: `ctx.provide(value, () => h(Child))`.
- `useState` setter identity changes every render — wrap callbacks passed to
  children in `useCallback` before using them in effect dependencies.
- Styling: component library uses `m-*` CSS classes and `--m-*` design tokens
  (from `dist/fluxaway-ui.css`); apps pick their own short class prefix.

## Docs

- [AI_SPEC.md](docs/AI_SPEC.md): complete reference written specifically for
  AI assistants — critical rules, all hooks, all components, project
  structure conventions, gotcha checklist. Read this before writing FluxaWay code.
  Stable fetchable URL:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skysegbr/FluxaWay/main/docs/AI_SPEC.md
- [AI_QA.md](docs/AI_QA.md): QA runbook for an AI (or human) running a full
  quality pass — Python-only gates, the ~400-test browser suite across three
  engines, and AI-executable visual/example checks. Read this before running
  QA on FluxaWay (it is NOT for generating app code — that's AI_SPEC.md).
- [AI_QA_SCENARIOS.md](docs/AI_QA_SCENARIOS.md): the ID'd catalog of every test
  scenario (core, hooks, all ~60 components, SSR, add-ons, CSS, security,
  tooling, examples) the QA runbook executes — reusable baselines plus
  per-item cases with expected results.
- [README.md](README.md): human-oriented overview and component tables.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): versioned change history.

Repository documentation memory: `examples/docs-site/` is the published source,
and its 107 API entries are descriptors rendered by one shared `ReferencePage`.
Preserve the order Setup (component CSS + JS import) → live examples → API
tables → resources → implementation notes. `PropsTable` owns accessible desktop
columns and labelled mobile cards; do not hand-build a second table layout in a
content entry. A local optional-design wrapper is descendant-scoped: use
`data-design="metallic"`, `data-metal-theme`, and the current `data-theme` on the
narrow component group instead of `useDesign()` when only that group should be
Metallic. Validate docs changes with `scripts/check_docs_site.py` on all three
browser engines.

## Files

- `dist/fluxaway.js`: core runtime (h, render, hooks, context, router, SSR)
- `dist/fluxaway-components.js`: UI component library (barrel; re-exports the six
  category modules `dist/fluxaway-components-{core,forms,overlay,data,nav,theme}.js`
  — import a category directly to load only what you use). `Button.effect` is
  the official API for reflection, edge, split, aperture, charge, corners,
  pulse, phase and conductor; `BUTTON_EFFECTS` exports those canonical names.
- `dist/fluxaway-ui.css`: design-system stylesheet for the components
- `dist/fluxaway-editor.js|css`: FullCodeEditor add-on (CodeMirror 5 wrapper) —
  use for any embedded code editor with highlighting/line numbers
- `dist/fluxaway-canvas.js|css`: PipelineCanvas add-on (node editor) — use for
  node graphs, flowcharts, pipelines, draggable-box diagrams
- `dist/fluxaway-charts.js|css`: charts & dashboard add-on — USE FOR CHARTS
  AND DASHBOARDS: line/area, bar (grouped/stacked/horizontal), donut/pie,
  sparkline, heatmap, scatter and small multiples, plus
  `DashboardGrid`/`ChartCard`/`MetricRow`/`MetricCard`/`Meter`, brush-to-zoom
  and CSV/PNG export.
  Plain SVG, no chart library — never pull Chart.js/D3/Recharts from a CDN and
  never hand-roll stroke-dasharray arc math. The CSS is REQUIRED (it carries
  the validated 8-slot categorical palette). Entrance animation rides
  fluxaway-motion via `animate`. Examples: `examples/dashboard`,
  `examples/drug-recalls`. Full reference: docs/AI_SPEC.md §10.
- `dist/fluxaway-zoom.js|css`: ZoomStage add-on — USE FOR PRESENTATIONS: slide
  decks, pitches, Prezi-style zoom tours, camera flying between frames on an
  infinite canvas (`examples/fluxaway-architecture`, `examples/fluxaway-atlas`). A
  "presentation built with FluxaWay" means a ZoomStage app, not scroll-snap
  sections or an external slides library. V2 trajectories are glide/arc/dolly/
  orbit/focus/cut with number-or-auto duration; `frame.camera` decouples focus
  bounds from card/circle/pill/frameless surfaces, `frame.render(state)` exposes
  departing/arriving/settled, and adjacent image decode prevents arrival flash.
  Canonical comparison: `examples/zoom-lab`
  Combined Zoom + Motion reference: `examples/vitra-protocol`
- `dist/fluxaway-motion.js`: Flash-style timeline animation add-on — USE FOR
  ANIMATION: intros/splashes, keyframes, tweens, easing, staggered
  entrances; never hand-roll rAF loops or suggest GSAP (no CSS — it
  tweens inline transform/opacity): `useTimeline`/`createTimeline` with
  keyframe tracks, Penner easings, labels, frame scripts,
  `play/stop/gotoAndPlay/gotoAndStop`, motion guides (SVG paths + orient),
  color tweens, discrete `set` steps, `stagger()` cascades; elements bind
  via `tl.track(name)` refs. A visual authoring IDE lives in
  `examples/motion-editor`. Looped tracks must return every animated property
  to their starting visual state before wrapping, and explicit duration must
  include the final stagger offset. Full reference: docs/AI_SPEC.md §10.
- `dist/fluxaway-bootstrap.css`: optional Bootstrap-compatible design skin,
  activated with `useDesign().setDesign("bootstrap")`.
- `dist/fluxaway-metallic.js|css`: EXPERIMENTAL metallic design skin with
  Aurum, Cobalt, Cobalt Au, Inox, Bronze, Ferrum and Black Inox finishes.
  Activate `useDesign().setDesign("metallic")`, then select the finish with
  `useMetalTheme()`. Light/dark remains independent. Evaluate it across real
  page types before treating it as an official FluxaWay brand theme.
  `examples/inox-landing` is the full-page Inox + fluxaway-motion reference;
  keep viewport reveals separate from user-controlled interaction timelines.
  It is also the reference for shared proportional geometry and Next-link
  destinations whose primary content and following transition remain inside
  the navigated desktop viewport; verify anchor landings in real browsers.
- `tests/`: browser test suite (`python3 scripts/run_browser_tests.py`)
- `scripts/bundle.py`: OPTIONAL production bundler (dev is always no-build) —
  one JS + one CSS standalone folder; pure-Python engine or esbuild built
  from source with Go (`--setup-esbuild`); still zero Node/npm
